strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with consistent improvements across multiple metrics and scenarios (30-34% FID improvement over CFLD)
Well-motivated problem with clear applications in AR/VR and robotics for understanding hand-object interactions from first-person perspective
Intelligent multimodal approach combining geometric cues (point clouds, 3D hand poses) with semantic information (textual descriptions)
Strong generalization demonstrated across unseen objects, actions, scenes, and subjects, plus real-world unlabeled examples
Thorough ablation studies validating the contribution of each modality component
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and generally well-written methodology
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (VAE, LDM, diffusion models) without fundamental innovation
Narrow domain scope: evaluation restricted to hand-object interaction tasks only; generalization claims to broader egocentric vision are overstated
Critical unaddressed dependency on accurate 3D hand pose estimation with insufficient robustness analysis for pose estimation failures and occlusions
Limited real-world validation: only qualitative results from single smartphone images without quantitative evaluation against ground truth
Conflicting evidence on text modality importance: Section A.2.2 shows reasonable performance with incorrect text, contradicting ablation findings about text necessity
Missing practical considerations: no discussion of computational cost, inference time, memory requirements, or real-time deployment feasibility
Lack of statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; improvements over CFLD on some metrics appear modest
Insufficient failure case analysis: limited investigation of systematic failure modes or guidance for detection/mitigation
Limited comparable baselines: few existing exocentric-to-egocentric methods; some compared methods not specifically designed for this task

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a practical need in egocentric vision, AR/VR, and robotics applications
Comprehensive and principled technical approach intelligently integrating multiple modalities (geometric, semantic, and appearance cues) through a coherent two-stage pipeline

Extensive experimental evaluation across 4 major datasets with diverse unseen scenarios, comprehensive metrics, and appropriate baselines showing consistent state-of-the-art improvements (~30% on unseen objects)
Thorough ablation studies systematically analyzing contributions of each conditioning modality and component, with robustness testing on incorrect text inputs
Demonstrated real-world generalization on in-the-wild iPhone images beyond controlled dataset scenarios
Clear presentation with well-designed figures effectively communicating the method and results
Strong qualitative results showing realistic hand-object interactions and semantic coherence in reconstructed egocentric views
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing off-the-shelf components (depth estimation, hand pose estimation, VLMs, diffusion models) rather than introducing new methods or theoretical contributions
Heavy dependence on external components with no analysis of how component failures cascade; method performance is bounded by component limitations
Insufficient analysis of failure modes—failure cases relegated to appendix with minimal discussion; unclear when/why method fails or how robust it is to component errors
Missing computational cost analysis critical for practical deployment; no discussion of inference time or memory requirements for the two-stage pipeline
Ad-hoc design choices lack proper justification (e.g., scale estimation formula in Eq. 3); sensitivity analysis for key hyperparameters missing
Limited evaluation on truly out-of-distribution scenarios—while in-the-wild results shown, only handful of examples; 'strong generalization' claims need more rigorous support
No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; some improvements are modest and statistical significance is not established
Camera parameter generalization unclear; assumptions about calibrated intrinsics and successful hand pose estimation not thoroughly discussed
Text guidance robustness analysis superficial; limited exploration of sensitivity to text quality variations beyond single incorrect description ablation
Code availability not mentioned; reproducibility would benefit from released implementation and trained models

strengths: Novel and well-motivated problem formulation addressing practical applications in AR/VR and robotics
Comprehensive experimental validation across 4 major datasets with multiple evaluation metrics and strong consistent improvements over baselines
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating the contribution of each component (pose, depth, text) to final performance
Clever integration of geometric and semantic information through a well-designed two-stage pipeline
Strong empirical results with substantial improvements (e.g., ~30% FID reduction, 3+ dB PSNR gains) demonstrating both effectiveness and robustness
Good generalization to unseen objects, actions, scenes, and subjects across multiple challenging scenarios
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and comprehensive technical documentation in appendix
Detailed analysis including robustness to incorrect text descriptions and comparison with multiple image completion backbones
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty in individual components - primarily combines existing techniques rather than introducing fundamental innovations
Missing comparisons with some recent exocentric-egocentric translation methods mentioned in related work (e.g., 4DIFf, ExoEgo-Gen)
Insufficient analysis of failure modes - limited systematic characterization of when/why the method fails and robustness under occlusions or extreme viewpoints
No discussion of computational efficiency, inference time, or real-time applicability despite motivation for AR/VR applications
Heavy dependency on quality of component predictions (depth estimation, hand pose, VLM) with limited analysis of graceful degradation
Limited real-world validation - primarily evaluated on controlled/scripted datasets with only few real-world examples
Scalability beyond hand-object interaction scenarios unclear - method specificity may limit broader applicability
Missing hyperparameter sensitivity analysis and limited justification for some design choices (pose representation, architectural configurations)
